title: Leaf litter: the wood drops food on its own floor
question: Same forest, same trees, same frame (11,000). A is what ships today; B is the identical run with abscission writing nothing, as it did before. Does the litter mat read as leaf litter, and is it the right amount? It roughly doubles a colony's food supply and costs 45% of mean frame time -- I would rather you set the amount than have me tune it to a number.
context_md: COUNTERS, because a floor with food on it looks the same whichever mechanism put it there: litter cells 11,478 total / 1,227 within three rows of the surface; at shade_death 0.0 both read exactly 0, so the counter is honest. Deliveries 238 -> 313 (+31%) in a paired ascii run whose control reproduces the pre-S4 numbers exactly. Mean frame 1.875 -> 2.714 ms (+45%), worst 38.8 -> 85.5. Colony-band food energy 600 -> ~58,000, which is about 50-65 ant-lifetimes for 52 ants -- food stops being scarce, and that invalidates the band creature_space was calibrated against. THE PALE CREAM LAYER IN BOTH IMAGES IS ROOTS, not litter; litter is the olive-yellow mat just under the canopy in A. Known gap: litter does not rot yet -- decay checks are keyed to a position and litter falls away from where it was shed, so it accumulates over a long game. The fix needs a scheduler change and I have not made it unasked.
